text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The English are shocked after Turkish soccer champions Fenerbahce beat Manchester United in the European champions' league -- United's first home defeat in 40 years in European competition.
- Fenerbahce shakes Europe with United win.
- Turkey becomes a powerful force in northern Iraq after the U.S. forces rival Kurdish groups to agree in meetings in Ankara.

- Tapes of secret meeting between rebel Turkish Kurd leader Abdullah Ocalan and Iraqi Kurdish warlord Jalal Talabani raise suspicions that late President Turgut Ozal was killed by hardliners because of his moderate views on the Kurds.
- Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan is trying to involve the government in the multi-million dollar business of organising tours for devout Moslems to make the Haj pilgrimage to Mecca.
- Holding companies race to buy ports to be sold off under the government's privatisation scheme.
- The government wants $8.5 million from the privatisation of state enterprises.
- Mothers were crying again -- this time for their sons who died in a rebel Kurds ambush in the southeastern province of Diyarbakir.
